bottlenecks.name: Orbit determination and uncertainty realism
bottlenecks.description: Maintaining catalogs and operator orbits with covariances that are actually realistic: atmospheric drag (the largest LEO prediction error), space-weather storms, sensor biases, unannounced maneuvers, data association and the shift from Gaussian to curved, non-Gaussian uncertainty over days. The May 2024 Gannon storm degraded collision prediction for days; ESA estimates ~54,000 objects >10 cm exist versus ~40,000 catalogued, and ~1.2 million 1-10 cm fragments are untracked.
bottlenecks.ondemand_math_help: Medium. Certified non-Gaussian propagation, bounded-error Pc and better drag-uncertainty models are expert-scarce applied math that on-demand capability makes routine (P1). But the binding constraint is data: no theorem detects an untracked fragment or forecasts a coronal mass ejection's arrival.

bottlenecks.name: Conjunction assessment and collision-avoidance operations
bottlenecks.description: Screening tens of thousands of objects against each other, computing Pc, deciding and coordinating maneuvers. Starlink performed 148,696 avoidance maneuvers Jun-Nov 2025 and 207,152 Dec 2025-May 2026 (over 40 per satellite per year) at a Pc threshold of 3e-7, 100x stricter than the 1e-4 industry norm. Cross-operator coordination is manual or bilateral; a Dec 2025 Chinese launch put a payload within ~200 m of a Starlink with no ephemeris sharing.
bottlenecks.ondemand_math_help: Medium-High for the mathematical parts: provably sound screening filters, verified coordination protocols, defensible thresholds (P2, P1). Low for the binding parts: data sharing, standards, US-China politics and conservative operator policy.

bottlenecks.name: Trajectory design and optimization
bottlenecks.description: Low-thrust, multi-body, cislunar and interplanetary trajectory design: initial-guess generation, local optimization, global search, invariant-manifold and low-energy transfers, contingency sets. Solved in principle, expensive in expert time; designs are locally optimal with unknown gaps.
bottlenecks.ondemand_math_help: High. This is the clearest 'solved in principle, expert-scarce' area. Pre-release agents already derive Pontryagin conditions and write shooting codes (HELIOS, Jul 2026); GTOC 12 agents doubled strategic scores in two years but failed on implementation details that stronger models plus verification fix. Moment-SOS methods are starting to give global-optimality certificates (Jul 2026).

bottlenecks.name: Onboard guidance and control, and GNC software verification
bottlenecks.description: Real-time convex and successive-convexification guidance (powered descent, rendezvous), attitude control, hybrid mode logic for docking and capture, learned controllers under runtime assurance, and the verification and validation that typically dominates flight-software cost. Proofs exist for idealized 3-DoF landing; 6-DoF guarantees, solver numerics and hybrid/contact logic are mostly validated by Monte Carlo and test.
bottlenecks.ondemand_math_help: High for proofs (convergence, feasibility, floating-point bounds, barrier certificates) via P1 and P2. The gates are specifications, tool qualification and certification acceptance, which compress far less than the cognitive work.

bottlenecks.name: Autonomous navigation
bottlenecks.description: Earth-independent navigation for cislunar and deep-space craft: optical and terrain-relative navigation, X-ray pulsar navigation, weak-signal GNSS at lunar distance (LuGRE fix on the Moon, Mar 2025), lunar PNT constellations (Moonlight, LunaNet) and their integrity guarantees.
bottlenecks.ondemand_math_help: Low-Medium. Integrity-certified filters and fault detection become cheap; accuracy remains set by sensors, clocks and signal geometry.

bottlenecks.name: Long-term dynamics and environment evolution
bottlenecks.description: Stability of cislunar and lunar orbits (frozen orbits, DROs, NRHOs, resonances), disposal-orbit safety, chaos and transport in three- and four-body models, and decade-scale debris-environment (Kessler cascade) modeling for capacity and licensing questions.
bottlenecks.ondemand_math_help: Medium for theory (computer-assisted transport bounds, proven thresholds in source-sink models), Low for operational change: chaos sets prediction horizons no proof removes, and debris models are dominated by uncertain inputs (fragmentation data, launch rates, compliance).

nodes.title: Formal astrodynamics library
nodes.description: Machine-checked definitions and core theorems for orbital mechanics (Kepler's equation, Lambert's problem, the circular restricted three-body problem and its Jacobi integral, Clohessy-Wiltshire relative motion, quaternion attitude kinematics, standard probability-of-collision definitions) in Lean or Isabelle, so GNC and traffic properties can be written as formal specifications.
nodes.status_oct2026: Essentially absent from Mathlib (general). Building blocks appeared in 2026: a Lean 4 Lyapunov-stability library for autonomous ODEs, Lean integral curves and flows on Banach manifolds (arXiv 2602.13247), and an agent pipeline that brought 84 of 175 statements of a numerical-ODE textbook to proof-complete Lean (arXiv 2606.14000, Jun 2026). No catalog family applies.
nodes.why: Every verified-GNC and verified-traffic chain below needs agreed formal definitions to state specifications against; today a team that wants to prove a guidance property must first formalize orbital mechanics itself. The openai/math pipeline produced agent-written Lean for 127 families in under four weeks; a core astrodynamics library is perhaps 10-30k lines (assumption), i.e. weeks of agent time under S2 rather than person-years. Parts touching numerical-integration error wait on infra-mathlib-applied.
nodes.strongest_case_small: Libraries are cheap; agreement is not. Definitions must match what flight-dynamics codes compute (reference frames, time systems, ephemerides, units), and the June 2026 audit found kernel-accepted agent formalizations with weakened hypotheses and parameter restrictions, so a library can compile and still misstate the physics.
nodes.signpost: A public Lean or Isabelle orbital-mechanics library covering Lambert, CR3BP and Clohessy-Wiltshire, adopted or cited by a NASA, ESA or university GNC group, by end-2027.

nodes.title: Catalog chaos results (weak link)
nodes.description: The openai/math families closest to orbital dynamics: positive metric entropy for the Chirikov standard map (146), counterexamples to strong forms of Arnold's fixed-point conjecture (347), sharp symplectic ball-packing criteria (343), and uniform limit-cycle bounds for planar polynomial vector fields (143). They concern model maps and planar fields, not the n-body problem.
nodes.status_oct2026: 146 is T1 (manuscript only); 347 is T3 (agent-written Lean, unchecked by outsiders); 343 is T1; 143 is T3. The release contains nothing on n-body dynamics, KAM theory for the three-body problem, or Arnold-diffusion rates.
nodes.why: Band refers to the results becoming established (T4 for the Lean families, outside endorsement for the manuscripts); their astro implication is separately judged nil-to-Low. The standard map is the textbook model of resonance overlap (Chirikov criterion), used heuristically to judge where near-resonant orbits turn chaotic; if 146 holds (conditional, T1), chaos there is measure-theoretically real, not a numerical artefact. 347 limits what periodic-orbit existence theorems can promise for Hamiltonian maps; 343 bounds symplectic phase-space packing. None yields a stability region, timescale or station-keeping number for a real orbit, so the downstream astro effect is confidence only (P5), conditional for 146 and 343.
nodes.strongest_case_small: No mission designer assumed the standard map was integrable; numerical chaos indicators (FLI, MEGNO, Lyapunov exponents) already guide practice, and these results change zero design decisions. Planar polynomial limit cycles (143) do not describe orbital dynamics at all.
nodes.signpost: Celestial-mechanics groups citing 146 or 347 in a three-body or resonance paper by 2028; if none do, treat the link as nil.

nodes.title: Rigorous n-body transport bounds
nodes.description: Computer-assisted proofs, with explicit constants, of transport, diffusion and escape-time bounds in realistic restricted and full three- and four-body models (Earth-Moon CR3BP, bicircular, ephemeris-forced), for example how long trajectories starting near a DRO or lunar frozen orbit provably stay bounded.
nodes.status_oct2026: Open frontier; not in the catalog. Capinski and Gidea gave a computer-assisted proof of Arnold diffusion in the planar full three-body problem for a Neptune-Triton-asteroid system (arXiv 2504.09273, Apr 2025): existence with explicit parameter ranges, not operational timescales. Practice relies on Monte Carlo propagation.
nodes.why: This is the bespoke, hard-but-not-famous problem class that analyst position (a) says the capability absorbs first. A single computer-assisted diffusion proof took a leading group years; at roughly 3 hours of compute per research result, a library of system-specific theorems (one per orbit family of operational interest) becomes cheap once outside teams have access. Value: replaces 'we ran 10^4 propagations' with 'no trajectory starting in set A leaves before time T', the form a disposal-orbit or parking-orbit safety case wants.
nodes.strongest_case_small: Proven bounds in chaotic regimes are usually orders of magnitude looser than observed behaviour (Nekhoroshev-type times are exponentially pessimistic), and solar gravity, radiation pressure and ephemeris perturbations break the clean models proofs need; operators will keep using Monte Carlo and active station-keeping.
nodes.signpost: An AI-assisted paper by 2028 proving explicit-time confinement or escape bounds for a real DRO, NRHO or lunar frozen-orbit family in a model that includes solar gravity.

nodes.title: Certified cislunar stability atlas
nodes.description: Validated (interval or Taylor-model) maps of where lunar frozen orbits, DROs, halo/NRHO families and resonant orbits stay bounded for 10-100 years, plus certified station-keeping delta-v budgets for stated navigation and maneuver-execution errors.
nodes.status_oct2026: Practice is numerical (Monte Carlo, chaos indicators). Verified propagation exists but reaches days to weeks in LEO (verified regularized Dromo interval propagation, TU Delft), not decades in chaotic regimes. ESA's Lunar Pathfinder targets a lunar frozen orbit; Moonlight navigation services are planned for end-2028 to 2030.
nodes.why: Long-lived lunar relay and navigation constellations (Moonlight: four navigation and one communication satellite), surface-base support orbits and disposal orbits need decade-scale budgets. A certified atlas turns propellant margins from 'Monte Carlo 99th percentile plus engineering margin' into a proven envelope; illustratively, halving a 20-30% station-keeping margin buys small relays years of life. It needs new theory plus verified numerics, so it lands a year after the pure proofs.
nodes.strongest_case_small: Chaos sets a hard horizon: NRHOs are unstable with prediction horizons of days to weeks, so no proof yields ballistic predictions beyond that; certified budgets then depend on controller and navigation-error models that are engineering assumptions. Frozen orbits and DROs are already known numerically to be stable enough for practice.
nodes.signpost: A lunar relay or navigation operator (ESA Moonlight, a CLPS relay provider) citing certified stability or station-keeping bounds in orbit selection or disposal planning.

nodes.title: Guarantees for convex landing guidance
nodes.description: Proofs of convergence, iteration bounds, recursive feasibility and robustness margins for the real-time guidance algorithms used in powered descent and proximity operations: lossless convexification beyond the 3-DoF case, 6-DoF successive convexification with state-triggered constraints, and robust or chance-constrained variants.
nodes.status_oct2026: Lossless convexification gives global optimality with deterministic convergence for 3-DoF powered descent (general; the Acikmese-Blackmore line of work behind G-FOLD and reusable-booster landing guidance). Successive convexification has convergence-to-stationarity guarantees via the prox-linear framework, extended to continuous-time, passively safe 6-DoF powered descent (Elango, Vinod, Di Cairano, Weiss, MERL TR2025-008, AIAA SciTech Jan 2025). Global optimality and worst-case iteration bounds for 6-DoF nonconvex problems remain open. No catalog family.
nodes.why: These are 'solved in principle, expert-scarce' problems: perhaps a few dozen groups worldwide write such proofs (general). On-demand research math turns each new constraint type (plume impingement, glideslope, sensor pointing, passive abort safety) into a same-week theorem instead of a dissertation chapter. Proven iteration bounds are what onboard schedulers need to guarantee a solution inside a fixed guidance cycle (roughly 1-10 Hz replanning for landing, general).
nodes.strongest_case_small: Reusable boosters already land routinely with convex/SCP-style guidance without global guarantees, relying on Monte Carlo campaigns and fallback logic; a proof changes paperwork, not landing accuracy, unless it lets designers cut propellant or divert margins.
nodes.signpost: AI-assisted proofs of recursive feasibility or iteration bounds for 6-DoF successive convexification published by a leading GNC group by end-2027.

nodes.title: Verified onboard optimization solvers
nodes.description: Embedded SOCP/QP solver code with machine-checked proofs that, in the flight processor's floating-point arithmetic, it terminates within N iterations and returns an epsilon-feasible, epsilon-optimal solution or a certified infeasibility flag.
nodes.status_oct2026: Pieces exist (verified floating-point analysis tools, formalized convex-optimization theory in Coq and Isabelle), but no verified SOCP solver has flown (general). Agent formalization of numerical analysis is immature: a June 2026 audit found that compilation-based metrics substantially overstate formalization quality (arXiv 2606.14000).
nodes.why: The flight risk in convex guidance sits less in the convex problem than in the implementation: conditioning, iteration caps, timeouts and floating-point rounding. A solver is roughly 5-20k lines (assumption), the size agent-written proofs can cover in weeks once S2's Mathlib numerics catch-up (2027-29) supplies the analysis library. Output: one reusable certified component for every lander, docking system and collision-avoidance planner.
nodes.strongest_case_small: Embedded solvers are small and tested by millions of Monte Carlo runs; numerical failures in flight are rare; DO-178C-style assurance can be met with testing and coverage without proofs, so programs may not pay to switch.
nodes.signpost: An open-source verified SOCP or interior-point solver with floating-point error bounds released by a lab or formal-methods group (NASA Formal Methods 2027/2028 or CAV).

nodes.title: Global optimality certificates
nodes.description: Methods that prove a low-thrust, multi-body or rendezvous trajectory is globally optimal, or within a stated percentage of the best possible, using moment/sum-of-squares relaxations, tight convex relaxations or rigorous branch-and-bound.
nodes.status_oct2026: Active and accelerating: differential-algebra Taylor expansions plus moment-SOS optimization with guaranteed convergence to the global optimum, demonstrated on low-thrust station-keeping in the Earth-Moon CR3BP (Evans, Fossa, Armellin, Henrion, Zanetti, arXiv 2607.15801, Jul 2026); sparse Lasserre hierarchy with GPU ADMM (STROM, arXiv 2406.05846). Scaling to many-revolution low-thrust transfers is open.
nodes.why: Flown low-thrust and multi-body designs are locally optimal from a designer's initial guess; nobody knows the gap to the global optimum. A certificate turns 'best we found' into 'within 0.5% of the best possible' and stops the global search. The open work is cognitive: exploiting sparsity and problem structure to keep the semidefinite programs tractable and proving when relaxations are exact.
nodes.strongest_case_small: SDP size grows combinatorially with relaxation degree and variable count, so certificates may stay limited to short-horizon or low-dimensional problems; the gaps found are typically a few percent of delta-v, which rarely changes what a mission can do.
nodes.signpost: A certified-global (or certified within 1%) solution to a GTOC-class or many-revolution low-thrust problem published by 2028.

nodes.title: Certified collision-probability math
nodes.description: Fast methods that propagate orbit uncertainty that has become non-Gaussian (curved, skewed, multimodal) and compute probability of collision (Pc) with rigorous error bounds, replacing the 2D Gaussian Pc shortcut where it fails.
nodes.status_oct2026: NASA CARA uses 2D Pc as the main risk input and brute-force Monte Carlo where 2D Pc is unreliable, and notes that Gaussian assumptions suppress the true non-Gaussian structure of position uncertainty. Differential-algebra, Gaussian-mixture and equinoctial-sampling methods exist without certified error bounds at catalog scale. Catalog 139 (subpolynomial-query log-concave sampling, T3) is a weak link: orbit-state posteriors are generally not log-concave.
nodes.premise_tier: n/a (139 is T3 and not load-bearing)
nodes.why: Starlink executed 148,696 avoidance maneuvers Jun-Nov 2025 and 207,152 Dec 2025-May 2026 (over 40 per satellite per year) at a Pc threshold of 3e-7, 100x stricter than the 1e-4 norm. Part of that conservatism is uncertainty about the uncertainty. Certified Pc bounds let operators replace margin-on-margin with a provable bound. Illustrative, not sourced: if conjunction Pc values spread roughly evenly across decades, a defensible move from 3e-7 to 1e-5 would remove on the order of 2-5x of maneuvers.
nodes.strongest_case_small: Pc error is dominated by input covariance realism (drag, unannounced maneuvers, sensor biases), not by the propagation method; a perfectly computed Pc from a wrong covariance is still wrong. Operators may keep strict thresholds for reputational and regulatory reasons regardless.
nodes.signpost: CARA, ESA CREAM or a commercial SSA provider adopting a bounded-error non-Gaussian Pc method in operational software by 2028.

nodes.title: Provably safe maneuver-coordination rules
nodes.description: Coordination protocols for independently operated autonomous fleets (right-of-way rules, maneuver-intent exchange, behaviour under communication loss) with machine-checked proofs that compliant fleets never maneuver into each other, plus game-theoretic analysis of non-cooperating operators.
nodes.status_oct2026: No standard exists. Starlink is autonomous within its own fleet; on Dec 9, 2025 a payload from a Chinese Kinetica-1 launch passed about 200 m from Starlink-6079 with no coordination or ephemeris sharing. TraCSS screens (52 pilot users plus UK and Australia accounts, about 11,125 satellites, Jun 2026) but does not arbitrate. Catalog 104 (quasipolynomial algorithms for mean-payoff, stochastic and parity games, T3) is a weak, theory-level link to synthesizing strategies for game models of such protocols.
nodes.premise_tier: n/a (104 is T3 and not load-bearing)
nodes.why: This is aviation's TCAS problem in orbit, and TCAS logic took years of formal analysis to trust. Multi-agent protocols with timing, message loss and asymmetric information are a natural target for agent-written proofs, which removes the expert-cost barrier. With about 13-14k active satellites today and filings for roughly 200k (China, Dec 2025) and up to 1 million (SpaceX orbital data centers, Jan 2026), pairwise human coordination cannot scale.
nodes.strongest_case_small: The binding problem is political and commercial (US-China data sharing, ITU, liability), not proof; a proven protocol nobody adopts is worthless, and bilateral API coordination between Western operators already works without proofs.
nodes.signpost: A CCSDS, ISO or CONFERS draft standard for machine-readable maneuver intent that includes a formal-verification annex, by 2028.

nodes.title: Cislunar tracking in chaotic dynamics
nodes.description: Orbit determination, initial orbit determination, sensor tasking and uncertainty propagation for non-Keplerian cislunar orbits (NRHO, DRO, L1/L2 halos, transfers) from sparse optical data, with proven consistency and custody guarantees.
nodes.status_oct2026: Earth-centric surveillance networks are not designed for cislunar space, and three-body dynamics make uncertainty dominate performance; more than 30 lunar missions are planned 2024-2030. AFRL's Oracle-Prime spacecraft passed a major milestone (Apr 2026), with delivery in 2026 and launch sought for 2027. NASA cancelled the Gateway station on Mar 24, 2026, removing the main planned NRHO traffic node.
nodes.why: Method development is cognitive and the expert community is small, so P1 is a large multiplier; but cislunar objects are faint and few sensors see them, so performance is capped by data. The math advance mainly lets a sparse sensor set keep custody with fewer observations.
nodes.strongest_case_small: Cislunar object counts stay in the tens through 2031, so manual analyst attention suffices; with Gateway cancelled, NRHO congestion is no longer a near-term driver.
nodes.signpost: Oracle-Prime launch (2027) and published custody performance; a Space Force or commercial cislunar object catalog.

nodes.title: Navigation filters with proven error bounds
nodes.description: Estimators for autonomous navigation (optical and terrain-relative, X-ray pulsar, GNSS at lunar distance, crosslink ranging) with machine-checked consistency and integrity bounds (protection levels), including non-Gaussian and sensor-fault cases.
nodes.status_oct2026: EKF/UKF variants dominate, tuned by experts; integrity frameworks are mature for aviation GNSS but not for lunar PNT. LuGRE tracked GPS and Galileo and obtained a navigation fix on the lunar surface (Mar 3, 2025); NASA's SEXTANT demonstrated real-time X-ray pulsar navigation (general). Catalog 140 (memory-sample lower bounds for noiseless Gaussian regression, T3) is a ceiling result (P3) for streaming estimation on memory-limited processors; 139 (T3) helps only where posteriors are log-concave.
nodes.premise_tier: T3 for the catalog pieces (140, 139); n/a for the main chain
nodes.why: Lunar PNT (Moonlight initial services end-2028, LunaNet interoperability tests 2029) needs integrity guarantees like aviation GNSS has. Proving filter consistency and fault detection under weak-signal geometry is bespoke applied math that on-demand capability makes routine.
nodes.strongest_case_small: Navigation accuracy is set by sensors and clocks (weak GNSS signals at lunar distance, pulsar photon counts giving kilometre-class XNAV fixes), not by filter proofs; proofs add assurance, not accuracy.
nodes.signpost: LunaNet or Moonlight integrity requirements specifying formally verified protection-level algorithms.

nodes.title: Verified docking and capture logic
nodes.description: Reachability and barrier-certificate proofs for rendezvous, proximity operations, docking and debris capture that cover mode switches, contact, sensor dropouts and learned (neural) controllers under runtime assurance.
nodes.status_oct2026: Neural-network-controlled spacecraft docking under Clohessy-Wiltshire dynamics is a standard verification benchmark (ARCH-COMP); scalable branch-and-bound verification of nonlinear neural feedback systems appeared in Sep 2026 (arXiv 2609.16298); AFRL flew neural-network attitude control of a satellite bus with watchdog and guardrail runtime assurance in shadow mode (Jul 28, 2026). NASA's revised Artemis III (2027) is a low-Earth-orbit rendezvous and docking test of Orion with the lander.
nodes.why: Hybrid verification is limited by state explosion and by the scarcity of people who can construct barrier certificates and decompositions; AI-generated certificates checked by a kernel are a near-ideal fit. It is also the route by which learned controllers, already flying under runtime assurance, gain static guarantees.
nodes.strongest_case_small: Contact dynamics (friction, compliance, plume impingement, capture-mechanism behaviour) is the uncertain part; a proof over an unvalidated contact model gives false confidence, and air-bearing and robotic hardware-in-the-loop tests remain the qualifying evidence.
nodes.signpost: A servicing or debris-removal operator (Astroscale, ClearSpace, Starfish) citing formal reachability proofs in a mission safety review.

nodes.title: Storm-proof drag forecasts
nodes.description: Physics-plus-data models of upper-atmosphere density and its uncertainty that keep LEO orbit predictions and covariances realistic through geomagnetic storms.
nodes.status_oct2026: Drag is the largest LEO prediction uncertainty. In the May 2024 Gannon storm LEO objects sank about 180 m per day, thousands of satellites maneuvered at once and collision prediction was degraded for days (Parker and Linares, arXiv 2406.08617). Consider-parameter methods fail to represent stochastic drag (UC3M work). Starlink is lowering its ~550 km shells to ~480 km during 2026, raising drag sensitivity.
nodes.why: AI can build better reduced-order density models and calibrated uncertainty (data assimilation with guarantees), the input that certified Pc needs. But density is sparsely measured and storm drivers (coronal-mass-ejection arrival time and magnetic orientation) are forecast at most a day or two ahead, so model gains saturate on observations. S3 gains a year through autonomous analysis of existing data, not through new physics.
nodes.strongest_case_small: The binding constraints are solar-wind forecasting and in-situ density data; neither moves with math. More satellites flying lower increases exposure faster than models improve.
nodes.signpost: The next G4-G5 storm: whether conjunction screening again degrades for days as in May 2024.

nodes.title: Kessler-threshold models with error bars
nodes.description: Long-term debris-environment models (source-sink and Monte Carlo) with proven stability thresholds (when runaway collisional growth starts) and honest uncertainty from fragmentation physics and compliance assumptions.
nodes.status_oct2026: MIT MOCAT (source-sink plus Monte Carlo, open-source pySSEM 2025) uses equilibrium stability as a capacity measure. ESA's 2026 report: more than 40,000 catalogued objects, about 54,000 larger than 10 cm and 1.2 million between 1 and 10 cm; LEO collision risk up 20% since 2024. The CRASH Clock (time to a likely collision if all maneuvering stopped) moved from 2.8 days in its Dec 2025 preprint to 5.5 days (vs 164 days in 2018) in the Jan 2026 revision, showing how assumption-sensitive headline metrics are.
nodes.why: Regulators face a SpaceX application for up to 1 million satellites (filed Jan 30, 2026) and roughly 200k Chinese ITU filings (Dec 2025); capacity questions need defensible math. Stability thresholds of source-sink ODE systems and their sensitivity are tractable applied math (P1); results reach practice as confidence about where the cliff is (P5). Band refers to the models existing with proofs and quantified uncertainty; the uncertainty band itself stays wide.
nodes.strongest_case_small: Outputs are dominated by inputs no theorem fixes: future launch rates, disposal compliance and fragment distributions drawn from a handful of hypervelocity tests. Estimates will span an order of magnitude regardless; Mach33's Oct 2025 analysis put a risk-based carrying capacity near 2.9 million objects, far above today's population.
nodes.signpost: An IADC-, FCC- or ESA-cited capacity study with proven thresholds and published sensitivity bands by 2028.

nodes.title: Proof-carrying GNC software toolchain
nodes.description: An engineering pipeline in which engineers write formal requirements and AI agents produce guidance, navigation, attitude-control and collision-avoidance code together with machine-checked proofs of stability, constraint satisfaction, timing and floating-point error bounds.
nodes.status_oct2026: NASA's FRET-to-Copilot chain turns structured requirements into runtime monitors; DO-333 gives aviation certification credit for formal methods; DARPA PROVERS (Collins) applies formal methods to autonomous air vehicles. Lean and agent workflows are not qualified tools, and no AI-produced proof is part of any flight-software safety case (general).
nodes.why: Verification and validation commonly consume around half of flight-software cost (general). Formal methods were limited by expert cost, not tools (analyst position b); the openai/math pipeline formalized the main results of 162 papers in weeks. Applied to GNC modules, proof cost per function falls from expert-weeks to agent-hours, putting verified GNC within reach of smallsat and startup teams, not only NASA.
nodes.strongest_case_small: Specifications become the bottleneck: a proof of the wrong property is worthless, and the June 2026 audit showed kernel-accepted formalizations with weakened hypotheses; the same failure in specifications would give false assurance at scale.
nodes.signpost: A NASA center, ESA or a major prime publishing a GNC module delivered with agent-written machine-checked proofs (NASA Formal Methods 2027 or 2028).

nodes.title: Trajectory design on demand
nodes.description: AI agents that take a mission description in plain language and return verified low-thrust, multi-body or low-energy trajectories (ballistic lunar transfers, manifold transfers, gravity-assist tours), with optimality certificates where available, in hours instead of the weeks to months of expert time typical today.
nodes.status_oct2026: Emerging before the release: HELIOS (arXiv 2607.24051, Jul 27, 2026) has an LLM derive Pontryagin conditions, check them symbolically, generate C++ shooting code and solve, compiling 11 of 11 scenarios from 8 to 48 variables. A GTOC 12 study (arXiv 2602.03630, Feb 2026) found strategic scores nearly doubled in two years (9.3 to 17.2 of 26) but agents failed on units, boundary conditions and debugging loops.
nodes.why: Trajectory design is solved in principle but expert-scarce (analyst position a): perhaps a few hundred specialists worldwide design multi-body low-thrust transfers (general). The GTOC 12 failure modes are exactly what stronger reasoning plus verification removes. Low-energy designs matter for small lunar missions: published work finds ballistic-transfer entries saving about 59 m/s over the best previously known transfers. Certificates (astro-global-optimality-certificates) strengthen but do not gate this node.
nodes.strongest_case_small: Trajectory design is perhaps 1-3% of mission cost (general); heritage tools (GMAT, MONTE, Copernicus, EMTG) already automate much of it; gains are speed and access for small teams, and delta-v gains of a few percent rarely change what a mission can do.
nodes.signpost: An AI agent placing top-3 in a GTOC with minimal human input, 2027-28; NASA or ESA flight-dynamics groups publishing agent-in-the-loop design workflows.

nodes.title: Certified screening for a million objects
nodes.description: Conjunction screening and risk software whose filters are proven never to discard a conjunction above threshold (under stated covariance assumptions), whose code is formally verified, and which scales to 100k to 1 million objects plus operator ephemerides.
nodes.status_oct2026: Screening runs on Space Force and commercial catalogs of roughly 35,000-40,000 tracked objects; TraCSS added on-demand bulk ephemeris screening for constellations (May 2025) and is onboarding operators, but the FY2027 request cuts the Office of Space Commerce from $52.5M to $11M.
nodes.why: Filter soundness (apogee-perigee, orbit-path and time filters) is a classic formal-methods target, and false negatives are a known risk class. The catalog will grow severalfold as sensors improve and constellations deploy (Starlink above 10,900; Amazon Leo in the hundreds; Guowang and Qianfan each planned above 10,000; orbital-compute fleets filed). Compute is not binding; trust in completeness is.
nodes.strongest_case_small: Screening already works at 40,000 objects; missed conjunctions come from untracked objects and poor covariances, not filter bugs, so verified screening mostly certifies what already works.
nodes.signpost: TraCSS, ESA or a commercial SSA firm publishing formal soundness proofs for its screening filters; the FY2027 Office of Space Commerce appropriation outcome.

nodes.title: Proven landing guidance flies
nodes.description: A powered-descent or docking guidance system whose convergence, feasibility and solver numerics are machine-checked, not only Monte Carlo-tested, flies on a lunar lander, a vertical-landing test vehicle or an RPO demonstrator.
nodes.status_oct2026: Convex and SCP guidance fly operationally without full proofs. NASA reshaped Artemis in Mar 2026: Artemis III in 2027 becomes a low-Earth-orbit rendezvous and docking test with the lander, with crewed landings targeted for 2028. CLPS landers fly several times a year.
nodes.why: Once a verified solver and toolchain exist (S2 2028), flight requires integration, software freeze and 12-24 months of test campaigns (general) plus a vehicle on the manifest. Cheapest first demos: terrestrial vertical-landing testbeds and smallsat RPO. Illustrative value: proven feasibility could let designers trim divert-propellant reserves, typically a few percent of descent propellant.
nodes.strongest_case_small: Flight teams trust Monte Carlo; adding proofs adds schedule risk; the first crewed landings use software frozen in 2026-27, so proven guidance reaches crewed landers no earlier than the 2030s.
nodes.signpost: A CLPS provider, university hopper or RPO demonstrator announcing guidance flight software with machine-checked convergence and numerics proofs.

nodes.title: Earth-independent nav with certified integrity
nodes.description: Flight demonstration of autonomous cislunar or deep-space navigation (optical, pulsar, lunar GNSS or LunaNet signals) whose filter carries machine-checked integrity bounds.
nodes.status_oct2026: ESA Moonlight: Lunar Pathfinder relay in a lunar frozen orbit from 2026, initial navigation services end-2028, interoperability tests 2029, full operations 2030. LuGRE proved GNSS fixes at the Moon (2025).
nodes.why: Navigation demos fly on their own schedule; the AI-math contribution is certified integrity in the filter, cheap in S2 by 2028. The first natural opportunity is the 2029 Moonlight/LunaNet interoperability campaign. S3 cannot beat the launch manifest, so S2 and S3 share a year.
nodes.strongest_case_small: Navigation programs may not prioritize formal integrity proofs; demos succeed or fail on sensor and clock hardware.
nodes.signpost: Moonlight or NASA lunar PNT program documents calling for formally verified integrity algorithms.

nodes.title: Servicing with a proven safety envelope
nodes.description: An autonomous servicing, inspection or debris-capture mission whose safety case includes formally verified keep-out zones, abort reachability and capture logic.
nodes.status_oct2026: Commercial servicing and debris-removal demonstrations are under way (general); ESA's CREAM programme is preparing in-orbit autonomous collision-avoidance demos; none uses formal proofs as primary safety evidence (general).
nodes.why: Proximity operations are where autonomy risk is highest and where verified hybrid logic is most valuable. Missions take 2-4 years from contract to launch (general), so proofs ready in 2028 meet a 2030 flight.
nodes.strongest_case_small: Mission safety reviews already accept test-based evidence; contact-model uncertainty limits what proofs certify.
nodes.signpost: A servicing mission (Astroscale, ClearSpace, Starfish or a government demonstrator) publishing a safety case built on formal verification.

nodes.title: Missions fly AI-designed trajectories
nodes.description: A lunar, cislunar or deep-space mission whose baseline trajectory and contingency set were produced primarily by an AI design agent and verified by the flight-dynamics team.
nodes.status_oct2026: None known as of Oct 2026.
nodes.why: Designs freeze 6-18 months before launch (general), and there are many small lunar and cislunar missions (more than 30 planned 2024-2030); if agents are trusted by 2027 (S2), a 2028 launch can fly one. S3 cannot compress the manifest, so it matches S2.
nodes.strongest_case_small: Attribution: flight-dynamics teams re-optimize in heritage tools, so the 'AI-designed' label may be cosmetic and the delta-v or time benefit marginal.
nodes.signpost: A mission press kit or AAS/AIAA paper crediting an AI agent for the baseline trajectory.

nodes.title: Proof-backed GNC in operational spacecraft
nodes.description: Operational uncrewed spacecraft (constellation satellites, landers, servicers) run GNC or collision-avoidance software whose safety case relies materially on AI-produced machine-checked proofs.
nodes.status_oct2026: None known. Formal methods in space flight software remain niche (NASA research programs, some ESA work). Commercial operators update fleet software frequently without regulator review of the code (general).
nodes.why: Uncrewed commercial systems need no tool qualification, so adoption is a cost decision: if proofs cut V&V cost and shorten update cycles, software-defined fleets adopt first. This precedes crewed certification by years.
nodes.strongest_case_small: Testing culture is entrenched and works; one high-profile incident with a 'proven' but mis-specified module could stall adoption.
nodes.signpost: An operator or prime stating publicly that flight GNC or collision-avoidance code ships with machine-checked proofs.

nodes.title: Autonomous cross-operator collision avoidance
nodes.description: Satellites of different operators (Starlink, Amazon Leo, OneWeb, Guowang, Qianfan, orbital-compute fleets) detect, negotiate and execute avoidance maneuvers autonomously under a shared protocol with formal safety guarantees, at 50,000-100,000-plus active satellites.
nodes.status_oct2026: Starlink is autonomous within its own fleet; ESA CREAM's AutoCA and AutoSTM components are in pilot use with in-orbit demos being prepared; cross-operator coordination is manual or bilateral; there is no US-China ephemeris sharing (Kinetica-1 near-miss, Dec 2025). Five moderate-to-high-risk Starlink conjunctions clustered on Aug 9-13, 2026, one reported at 24% Pc.
nodes.why: The verification math is ready around 2028 in S2. Standards (CCSDS or ISO, typically 3-5 years, general), license conditions (FCC) and software rollout set the date; among US and European operators 2030 is plausible. Inclusion of Chinese constellations is a geopolitical gate the math cannot move. Capped at Medium because it needs regulator and standards acceptance.
nodes.strongest_case_small: Bilateral automation between Western operators will arrive without formal guarantees and will handle most of the risk; proofs add assurance, not capability.
nodes.signpost: A public automated maneuver-coordination agreement between two megaconstellation operators; an FCC license condition requiring machine-readable maneuver intent.

nodes.title: Cislunar traffic management service
nodes.description: An operational catalog, conjunction-screening and coordination service for cislunar space (low lunar orbit, NRHO, DRO, transfers, Earth-Moon L1/L2), comparable to TraCSS for LEO.
nodes.status_oct2026: None operational. Gateway cancelled (Mar 24, 2026) in favour of a roughly $20B lunar surface base over seven years; Moonlight relay and navigation services 2028-2030; Oracle-Prime demonstration launch sought for 2027.
nodes.why: Algorithms are ready by 2028-29 in S2; space-based cislunar sensors and a funded operator are the gates, and US civil SSA funding is under pressure (Office of Space Commerce FY2027 request down about 80%). A basic military or commercial service is plausible by 2031.
nodes.strongest_case_small: Cislunar traffic remains tens of objects; demand for a formal service may lag the capability; Gateway's cancellation removes the most congested planned orbit.
nodes.signpost: A Space Force, NASA or commercial announcement of a cislunar catalog or screening service; extension of TraCSS-like screening beyond GEO.

nodes.title: AI proofs accepted for crewed GNC
nodes.description: NASA human-rating, FAA commercial human-spaceflight rules or ECSS accept AI-produced machine-checked proofs as certification evidence for crew-critical GNC (landing, docking, abort).
nodes.status_oct2026: Aviation's DO-333 gives formal-methods credit, but Lean and agent workflows are unqualified tools; there is no precedent for AI-generated certification evidence in human spaceflight (general). The first crewed Artemis landings (targeted 2028) will use software frozen before such evidence exists.
nodes.why: Certification regimes move on their own clock: formal-methods credit in aviation took years after DO-333 (2011) to become routine (general). Even in S3, human-rating requires flight heritage of the uncrewed version and qualified tooling, so the physical and institutional clock binds.
nodes.strongest_case_small: Crewed GNC is a small share of flight software and already has a strong safety record; the gain is cheaper assurance, not safer missions.
nodes.signpost: NASA or FAA guidance (a technical-standard update or advisory-circular draft) addressing AI-generated formal evidence.

nodes.title: LEO stays safe at 100k satellites
nodes.description: Collision risk and avoidance-maneuver burden per satellite stop rising, and begin to fall, while the active LEO population grows 3-10x toward 50,000-100,000-plus.
nodes.status_oct2026: Maneuvers per Starlink satellite rose to more than 40 per year (Jun 2025-May 2026), with yearly totals more than 3x 2024; ESA puts LEO collision risk up 20% since 2024; close approaches under 1 km occur every 22 minutes in the 550 km Starlink shell (Thiele et al.).
nodes.why: AI math contributes three levers: certified Pc (fewer false alarms), verified coordination (no maneuver-into-each-other events) and better capacity models. But the dominant residual risk is about 1.2 million untracked 1-10 cm fragments that no math can see, plus drag-forecast limits and non-cooperating operators. The physical gate (sensors that track smaller objects, and their deployment) binds, so even S2 does not deliver this by 2031.
nodes.strongest_case_small: Most per-satellite risk reduction will come from non-math moves already under way: lower altitudes (Starlink 550 to 480 km, cutting ballistic decay time by over 80% at solar minimum), five-year disposal rules and better sensors.
nodes.signpost: Starlink semiannual reports showing maneuvers per satellite flat or falling while the fleet grows; ESA's 2027-28 environment reports showing LEO risk growth slowing.

nodes.title: Capacity-based orbital licensing
nodes.description: Regulators (FCC, national agencies, eventually ITU) license megaconstellations against an aggregate, model-based orbital capacity or risk budget, using verifiable debris-evolution and conjunction models.
nodes.status_oct2026: The FCC has a five-year post-mission disposal rule (2022) but no aggregate capacity regime; the FCC Space Bureau accepted SpaceX's up-to-1-million-satellite orbital data center application for filing in Feb 2026; China filed for roughly 200k satellites at the ITU (Dec 2025).
nodes.why: Filings at the million-satellite scale force a capacity framework this decade regardless of AI. AI math changes whether the framework rests on defensible, auditable models (proven thresholds, verified screening) or on rules of thumb. Rulemaking (notice, comment, order) takes 2-4 years (general). Capped at Medium.
nodes.strongest_case_small: Policy will be set by politics and spectrum economics; regulators can adopt simple per-operator rules without sophisticated models.
nodes.signpost: An FCC notice of proposed rulemaking or license condition using an aggregate collision-risk or capacity metric, triggered by the 1-million-satellite application.

nodes.title: Verified autonomy becomes cheap
nodes.description: At early adopters, the cost and calendar time of verifying GNC and autonomy software fall by half or more, making formally assured autonomy standard for smallsats and commercial landers rather than a NASA-only luxury.
nodes.status_oct2026: Formal methods are confined to a few high-value programs (general).
nodes.why: If V&V is roughly half of flight-software cost (general) and agent-written proofs replace a substantial share of test-based evidence for GNC modules, early adopters could halve assurance cost. Commercial uncrewed fleets realize it first; regulated crewed programs last.
nodes.strongest_case_small: Proofs add new costs (specification writing and review, independent checking); hardware test campaigns remain; net savings could be modest.
nodes.signpost: Published cost data from an operator or NASA program comparing proof-based versus test-based assurance for a GNC module.

scenario_contrast: S1 (Plateau): research-grade math reaches outside teams around 2027-28 but stays mostly in proofs; the domain's one robust effect by 2031 is trajectory design on demand (High), with first missions flying AI-designed trajectories around 2029. Verified solvers, proof-carrying GNC toolchains and certified screening appear around 2030 as research artifacts (Medium); nothing at tier 6-7 beyond flown trajectories is more than Low. S2 (Exponential, base case): the cognitive clock collapses tiers 1-4 into 2027-2028 - SCP guarantees, certificates, certified Pc, verified solvers, coordination protocols, hybrid docking proofs and the GNC toolchain are all High by 2031. Then the physical clock takes over: flight demos land in 2029-2030 (Medium) because of software freezes, test campaigns and manifests; operational proof-backed uncrewed GNC (2029) and cross-operator autonomous collision avoidance (2030) are Medium, the latter capped by standards and regulators; crewed certification credit and 'LEO safe at 100k satellites' stay Low because tool qualification, untracked debris and geopolitics bind. S3 (Recursive) pulls every cognitive node to 2027 and buys about one year at tiers 5-6 (e.g. landing-guidance demo 2028, proof-backed ops 2028), but launch cadence, design-freeze cycles, sensor deployment, standards bodies and US-China coordination move barely at all: several tier 5-6 nodes (AI-designed trajectories flown, autonomous navigation demo) have the same year in S2 and S3. The gap between the cognitive frontier and flown capability widens with each scenario: in S2 it is roughly 2-3 years; in S3 3-4 years.
key_insights: Start from the field: astrodynamics' math effort sits in orbit-determination uncertainty, conjunction operations, trajectory design and GNC verification - bespoke applied math, not famous conjectures. The catalog families nearest the domain (146, 347, 343, 143) concern model maps and planar fields; their astro effect is confidence-only and near nil. The lever is the capability (P1) and formal verification (P2).

The fastest real effect is trajectory design on demand: it was visible before the release (HELIOS, Jul 2026; GTOC 12 agents doubling strategic scores in two years) and needs no regulator. High by 2031 in every scenario; flown AI-designed trajectories by 2028 in S2.

Verified GNC is the highest-value chain: SCP convergence proofs -> verified onboard solvers -> proof-carrying GNC toolchain -> flight demo -> operational uncrewed use. In S2 the math is done by 2028, flight demos 2029, operational uncrewed use 2029; crewed certification credit stays Low through 2031 because tool qualification and human-rating clocks bind.

Space traffic is data- and politics-bound, not math-bound: ~1.2 million untracked 1-10 cm fragments, drag forecasts limited by space weather, and no US-China ephemeris sharing (Dec 2025 near-miss at ~200 m). Certified Pc and verified screening can cut false alarms (Starlink maneuvers at 3e-7, 100x stricter than the norm, ~355k maneuvers a year) only if covariances are realistic.

The cognitive clock compresses tiers 1-4 by 2-3 years from S1 to S2; tiers 5-7 move 1-2 years at most, and S3 adds about one more year. Launch manifests, design freezes, test campaigns, standards bodies and sensor deployment are the binding gates for every tier 5-7 node.

Chaos sets hard horizons that no proof removes: unstable cislunar orbits like NRHOs have prediction horizons of days to weeks. AI math can certify where orbits are regular and bound station-keeping given a controller model, but Monte Carlo and active control remain.

Cislunar math will arrive before cislunar traffic: Gateway's cancellation (Mar 24, 2026) removes the main NRHO traffic node; cislunar object counts stay in the tens; the gate for a traffic service is funded sensors, not algorithms.

The new failure mode is specification error: a June 2026 audit showed kernel-accepted agent formalizations with weakened hypotheses and parameter restrictions. For flight software, a proof of the wrong property gives false assurance at scale, so specification review and independent checking become the scarce resource.
nil_effects: No catalog result changes an orbit, maneuver or trajectory: 146, 347, 343 and 143 concern the standard map, Hamiltonian fixed points, symplectic packing and planar polynomial fields; the release has no n-body, KAM-for-three-body or Arnold-diffusion-rate results.

Chaotic prediction horizons (Lyapunov times of days to weeks for NRHO-type orbits) are a property of the dynamics; proofs cannot extend ballistic predictability, so station-keeping and Monte Carlo remain.
Untracked debris: about 1.2 million 1-10 cm fragments cannot be screened against; detecting them needs sensors, not mathematics.

Delta-v physics: the rocket equation and multi-body energetics are fixed; global-optimality certificates typically expose gaps of a few percent, and low-energy transfers trade flight time for propellant rather than giving it free.
Space-weather forecast lead time (coronal-mass-ejection arrival and orientation) limits storm-time drag prediction regardless of model sophistication.
Launch cadence, design-freeze cycles and lander schedules (Artemis III as a 2027 LEO docking test, crewed landings targeted 2028) are set by hardware and programs, not by AI math.
Coordination with non-cooperating operators (including US-China data sharing) is a political gate; a provably safe protocol does nothing if one fleet does not run it.
Galactic speedups in the release (matrix multiplication exponent, sub-n-log-n FFT) give no practical speedup to orbit propagation, screening or onboard estimation codes.
Hardness results such as Unique Games (102) bound worst-case fleet-scale tasking, but individual collision-avoidance maneuver planning is small and solved per event, so the ceilings do not bind.
Navigation accuracy at the Moon and in deep space is set by sensors, clocks and signal geometry; certified filters change assurance, not accuracy.

signposts.event: Public availability (API or product) of a research-grade math model from any lab, with pricing usable by aerospace teams.
signposts.what_it_changes: Starts every P1 chain (SCP guarantees, transport proofs, global certificates, trajectory design on demand); its date is the main S1-versus-S2 discriminator. If later than mid-2028, shift S2 tier 2-4 years right by about one year.

signposts.event: An AI agent places top-3 in a Global Trajectory Optimization Competition (GTOC) with minimal human input (2027-28).
signposts.what_it_changes: Confirms trajectory design on demand and flown AI-designed trajectories (High). Failure due to the same implementation errors found in the GTOC 12 study would push those nodes a year later.

signposts.event: First independent Comparator check of openai/math Lean families, including 347, 143, 104, 139 and 140.
signposts.what_it_changes: Moves those families from T3 to T4; mainly tests the verification pipeline that astro verification chains rely on, since their direct astro effect is small.

signposts.event: Release of a public formal astrodynamics library or a verified embedded SOCP/QP solver with floating-point bounds (e.g. at NASA Formal Methods 2027).
signposts.what_it_changes: Confirms the verified-GNC chain is on the S2 track (toolchain 2028, flight demo 2029). Absence by end-2028 moves those nodes toward S1 timing.

signposts.event: Starlink's next two semiannual FCC reports (maneuvers per satellite; currently over 40 per year and rising).
signposts.what_it_changes: If per-satellite maneuvers flatten while the fleet grows, better covariances and Pc methods are biting (raise astro-leo-safety-at-scale). Continued tripling means data and coordination bind (keep Low).

signposts.event: FCC action on SpaceX's up-to-1-million-satellite orbital data center application, and the FY2027 appropriation for the Office of Space Commerce (request $11M vs $52.5M).
signposts.what_it_changes: An aggregate risk or capacity metric in an FCC order raises astro-capacity-licensing; a gutted TraCSS lowers astro-catalog-scale-screening adoption and cislunar traffic management.

signposts.event: First automated cross-operator maneuver-coordination agreement (e.g. Starlink with Amazon Leo) or a CCSDS/ISO maneuver-intent standard draft.
signposts.what_it_changes: Confirms the regulatory gate is moving for astro-autonomous-ca-at-scale; inclusion of a Chinese operator would be a major upside surprise.

signposts.event: NASA or FAA guidance on AI-generated formal evidence for flight software, or the first DO-178C/DO-333 credit for AI-produced proofs in aviation.
signposts.what_it_changes: The leading indicator for infra-tool-qualification and astro-human-rated-proof-credit; without it, crewed credit stays Low or Speculative in every scenario.
Shows whether storm-time screening still degrades for days as in May 2024; a materially better outcome would raise astro-thermosphere-drag-uq.
